questions.question: Which of the following statement is NOT generally used in structured programming?
questions.explanation: goto jumps to a label anywhere in the function, breaking the single-entry, single-exit rule of structured programming. break, continue and switch all fit structured constructs, so goto is the exception.

questions.question:
How many times will the following loop execute?
for(j = 1; j <= 10; j = j - 1)
questions.explanation: j starts at 1 and j = j - 1 moves it further from the limit, so j <= 10 stays true and the loop never ends. A loop whose counter moves away from the test is infinite.

questions.question: A do while loop is useful when we want that the statements within the loop must be executed -
questions.explanation: do-while tests its condition after the body, so the body runs before the first test and therefore executes at least once even when the condition starts out false.

questions.question: The break statement is used to exit from -
questions.explanation: break leaves the nearest enclosing loop or switch at once. An if block is not a loop, so break cannot be used to leave it, and it does not end the program by itself.

questions.question: Which of the following is an exit controlled loop?
questions.explanation: do-while is the only exit-controlled loop in C because its test sits at the bottom. while and for are entry-controlled: they test first and may run zero times.

questions.question: The continue statement cannot be used with -
questions.explanation: continue belongs to loops: it jumps to the next iteration of for, while or do-while. switch is a selection construct, so continue has no meaning inside it.

What happens if a break statement is omitted in a switch-case block in C?

options.C: Execution falls through to the next case

questions.explanation: Without a break, control falls through into the following case bodies and keeps running until a break or the end of the switch. This fall-through is a well-known source of bugs.

questions.question:
How many times will the following loop body execute?
for(int i = 0; i < 5; i++) { }
questions.explanation: i takes the values 0, 1, 2, 3 and 4; once i becomes 5 the test i < 5 fails. That is five executions of the body in total.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of times a do-while loop body executes?
questions.explanation: The body runs before the condition is tested, so the minimum is one execution even when the condition is false from the very start. That is the difference from a while loop.

questions.question: In C, the else clause associates with -

options.B: The nearest unmatched if above it

questions.explanation: An else always binds to the nearest unmatched if above it, whatever the indentation suggests. Braces are needed when it should belong to an outer if.

questions.question: Which section of the for loop is optional in C?
questions.explanation: Initialisation, condition and update are all optional, and for(;;) is a legal infinite loop. Only the two semicolons are compulsory.

What does the continue statement do inside a for loop?

options.B: Skips the current iteration and moves to the next
options.C: Restarts the loop from the beginning

questions.explanation: continue skips the rest of the current pass and jumps to the update part of a for loop (or the test of while/do-while). The loop itself keeps running.

questions.question: Which data type CANNOT be used as a switch expression in C?
questions.explanation: switch needs an integer-compatible controlling expression such as int, char, short, long or enum. float and double are rejected because exact comparison of fractions is unreliable.
